newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Meralco 9-mth profit seen at 4.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Meralco 9-mth profit seen at 4.0 bln.

text.p: Manila Electric Co (Meralco) is likely to post profits of about 4.0 billion pesos in the first nine months of 1996 from 3.34 billion pesos in the same period last year, analysts said on Tuesday.
The profit rise would be spurred by 10 percent growth in sales volume from last year's 11.90 billion kilowatt-hours (kwh), they said.
Meralco is the Philippines' biggest electricity distributor, controlling 75 percent of the market in the northern island of Luzon with 2.8 million customers.
"Among the index heavyweights, Meralco has been one of those performing within expectation," said Helen Alvarez, vice-president for research at Citytrust Investment Bank.
"With increased sales and improved systems loss, the company will likely post 3.8 billion (pesos) for the first nine months," she said.
Alvarez put the rise in sales volume at 10.6 percent for the first nine months as well as for the full year.

"Meralco should be posting a net income of 1.3 billion pesos for the third quarter alone and we see it having the same sales volume growth as it did in the second quarter," said Alex Pomento, analyst at Baring Securities (Phils) Inc.
Meralco posted 2.37 billion pesos in profits for the first half of this year with sales volume rising by 10.6 percent to 8.5 billion kwh.
Alvin Ang of All Asia Capital said the firm was likely to see profits of 4.3 billion pesos for the nine months. He put full-year profits at 5.7 billion pesos compared with 4.4 billion last year.
Benito de la Cruz, Meralco's senior vice-president for finance, told Reuters on Tuesday the company would probably meet its nine-month electricity sales growth target of 10 percent.
The company group had set a target of eight to 10 percent for the full year.
"With the growth of over 10 percent for the first eight months, the 10 percent looks like an achievable target for the first nine months," de la Cruz said.
